hero.headline: The National Standard for Site Readiness
paragraphs: Companies making location decisions move fast and eliminate sites early. Most sites are not ruled out because they are bad sites. They are ruled out because key information is missing, unclear or unverified when a site selector needs it.

REDI Sites is the first national site readiness designation program in the United States, developed in affiliation with the Site Selectors Guild. Every site that completes the process receives a designation reflecting its current level of investment readiness, telling site selectors exactly where it stands, and telling you what to do next.

statementOfValue.heading: Statement of Value
paragraphs: At REDI Sites, we specialize in representing the readiness of commercial properties for development, providing clear and transparent evaluations that help streamline project planning. Our expert team assesses key factors such as infrastructure, zoning compliance, and environmental conditions to deliver precise insights that support effective time-to-market strategies.

By offering detailed reports and ongoing project management support, we help investors and developers reduce uncertainty and accelerate decision-making. Our transparent approach ensures all stakeholders have a clear understanding of site potential and challenges, enabling smoother coordination and faster project execution.

Choosing REDI Sites means partnering with a team committed to enhancing transparency and efficiency throughout the development process. We empower clients to make informed decisions quickly, minimizing delays and maximizing the value of their commercial real estate investments.

mission.heading: Bringing Greater Confidence to Site Selection
paragraphs: Every community wants to demonstrate that its sites are "ready" for investment. But across the United States, there is no universal definition of what "site ready" actually means.

REDI Sites was created to establish a more consistent, transparent, and investment-focused standard for evaluating industrial properties. Rather than serving as another marketing designation, REDI Sites provides an objective framework that helps communities better prepare sites while giving companies greater confidence in the locations they evaluate.

Each designation combines engineering analysis with independent review by experienced site selection consultants, ensuring sites are evaluated through both technical and real-world corporate investment perspectives. The result is a more disciplined evaluation process that helps reduce uncertainty, identify potential risks earlier, and accelerate investment decisions.

Developed as an initiative of the Site Selectors Guild, REDI Sites reflects decades of experience advising corporations on major location decisions and translating those lessons into practical standards that benefit both communities and investors.

businessModel.heading: The Experts Behind REDI Sites
paragraphs: REDI Sites was developed by the Site Selectors Guild, the world's foremost association of professional site selection consultants.

Guild Members are independent advisors who help companies identify, evaluate, and select locations for major business investments around the world. Every Guild Member has earned the Certified Site Selection Consultant (CSSC) credential and is bound by a Code of Ethics emphasizing objectivity, confidentiality, and professional judgment.

Unlike organizations that promote communities, Guild Members represent the interests of corporate investors. Their collective experience evaluating hundreds of projects each year ensures REDI Sites reflects how companies actually assess investment readiness, not simply how sites are marketed.

guildMission.heading: Site Selectors Guild Mission & Vision
guildMission.mission: To advance the practice of site selection while helping companies make smarter location decisions and supporting communities in creating environments where investment can succeed.
guildMission.vision: A world where communities and corporate investors share a common understanding of investment readiness, resulting in faster decisions, reduced risk, and stronger economic outcomes.

whyGuild.heading: Why the Site Selectors Guild Created REDI Sites
paragraphs: Communities have invested heavily in preparing industrial sites for development, but over time, "site readiness" has come to mean different things to different organizations.

Some programs emphasize environmental due diligence. Others focus on utilities, transportation, permitting, or marketing. While each provides value, the lack of a common standard can create uncertainty for companies evaluating locations.

The Site Selectors Guild recognized this growing disconnect between corporate expectations and community definitions of readiness. REDI Sites was developed to establish a consistent, credible framework rooted in real-world corporate site selection experience. Rather than replacing existing site readiness efforts, REDI Sites complements them by introducing an independent, investment-oriented perspective based on the criteria companies and their advisors evaluate every day.
The result is greater confidence for investors, greater clarity for communities, and a more efficient site selection process for everyone involved.

hero.heading: The Standard
hero.body: A site is rarely eliminated for being a bad site. It is eliminated when the information a site selector needs is missing, unclear, or unverified. Here is how REDI Sites evaluates that and what your site needs to participate. REDI Sites is industry- and use-agnostic. The evaluation focuses on the foundational factors that influence whether a site can advance with greater speed, certainty, and fewer surprises, regardless of the project ultimately considering it.

methodology.heading: Every Site, Reviewed Twice
paragraphs: Your documentation is reviewed first by Terracon, an independent engineering firm, and then by REDI Reviewers, practicing site selectors who confirm the final score and designation.
There is no pass or fail. Every site that completes the process receives a designation on a 10-point readiness index, along with a report showing where it is strong and where gaps remain.

process.heading: The Designation Process

steps.label: Register
steps.description: Once registered, applicants submit documentation across five weighted categories of readiness through Lasso, an online property data collection database.

steps.label: Submit your RFI and documentation
steps.description: Answer the RFI and upload exhibits covering the scored categories.

steps.label: Engineering Review
steps.description: Your documentation goes to Terracon, the program's independent third-party engineering reviewer.

steps.label: REDI Review
steps.description: REDI Reviewers, practicing Site Selectors Guild members, review the Terracon report and have final decision authority on the site's score and designation level.

steps.label: Designation
steps.description: The site receives a feedback report, marketing materials and a listing in the REDI Sites database. Sites may use the REDI Sites logo and the logo for their designation level.

process.footnote: Designations are valid for one year. As additional due diligence is completed, a site can be resubmitted and redesignated at a higher level.

criteria.heading: How Sites Are Scored
criteria.body: Each site receives a score from 0 to 10 based on the documentation submitted across five weighted sections. Within each section, individual categories carry their own weights. The section weights reflect what matters most to companies and the site selectors who advise them.
